newsitem.title: USA: Hughes' DirecTV says Dec. sales best ever.
newsitem.headline: Hughes' DirecTV says Dec. sales best ever.

text.p: DirecTV, the satellite television division of giant Hughes Electronics Inc on Thursday said it capped 1996 with its best month ever for signing up subscribers.
The company enrolled 165,000 new members in its direct broadcast satellite business versus the most recent monthly record of 125,000, set in September 1996.

"A lot has been written about a perceived slowdown in our business," Ed Hartenstein, chief executive officer, said at a press conference at the Winter Consumer Electronics Show here. "But this was one of the strongest sales seasons we've seen."

Overall, the DirecTV's subscriber base rose to 2.3 million members after adding roughly 1.12 million net new subscribers in the year. In 1995, the company added 900,000 new subscribers, Hartenstein said.

He said DirecTV would continue its $200 rebate program through February. The plan has lowered the net cost of a DirecTV digital broadcast system to around $199.00, a price that has "driven an incredible amount of floor traffic" in retail stores, Hartenstein said.
No definitive decision has been made on whether the company will further extend the rebate program, which was begun in August 1996.

For 1997, DirecTV is working with computer software companies like Microsoft Corp and hardware companies like International Business Machines Corp to build the necessary equipment to put a DirecTV service on a home PC. By doing so, the PC could receive television signals, as well as download some World Wide Web pages from the Internet and receive data, enhanced video and other information.
